paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is about. These brothers walk into Egypt to buy grain. But the real thing on the table is what they did to Joseph. Under pressure, it comes out of their mouths (Genesis 42:21).

Look at what they say to one another: "Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen." (Genesis 42:21). Right there, it's clearly on their minds. And Reuben says, "Now we must account for his blood!" (Genesis 42:22). I think that tells us something true, baker: what we've done can catch up with us when life squeezes.

But look who else is in this passage. Joseph recognizes them, and I think he turns away and weeps because it still matters to him (Genesis 42:24). And he says, "I fear God" (Genesis 42:18). So the story isn't only about guilt. It's about a God who is working while people are afraid and confused, and the story isn't over. So if something is heavy on your heart today, baker, bring it into the light now, because carrying it alone is a LOT heavier than I ever carried those cookie boxes.
